controls.capability: Information-security policies enforced through release-blocking configuration and governance gates
Security responsibilities assigned through owner authorization and organization-scoped operations
Segregation of duties through owner allowlists, strict reverification, and approval boundaries
Access control policy implemented through tenant, product, plan, quota, and owner authorization
Identity lifecycle uses Clerk organizations, passwordless authentication, session binding, and revocation
Authentication information protected through passkeys, verified email, key rotation, and secret non-disclosure
Access rights reviewed and changed through owner operations, service disablement, and revocation controls
Cloud-service security governed through Vercel deployment parity, runtime monitoring, and fail-closed storage
Incident preparation includes token, session, organization, and service containment mechanisms
Evidence is preserved through immutable release records, idempotent events, and auditable control mappings
ICT continuity supported through rollback evidence, multi-target deployments, and performance isolation
Security awareness is represented through governed owner workflows and documented operational controls
Privileged access requires owner allowlisting and recent strict reverification
Secure authentication uses passwordless methods, passkeys, enterprise SSO, and high-risk step-up
Configuration management validates identity policies, token key rings, service credentials, and storage settings
Data leakage prevention includes no-store responses, secret redaction, bounded telemetry, and browser identifier restrictions
Security events are logged without credentials, tokens, or session identifiers
Monitoring includes runtime error scans, health status, abuse detection, and distributed validation rate limits
Cryptography includes HMAC signing, constant-time verification, key identifiers, and controlled rotation
Secure development lifecycle is enforced through security, supply-chain, privacy, resilience, and release gates
Secure coding is validated through TypeScript builds, linting, source-integrity tests, and bounded input handling
Security testing is mandatory before release and repeated against deployed systems
Change management uses branch validation, preview deployments, release evidence, and rollback checks
